units.leftText: Paul, an apostle—not from men, nor through man, but through Jesus Christ, and God the Father, who raised him from the dead—
units.rightText: Paul, an apostle (not from men, neither through man, but through Jesus Christ, and God the Father, who raised him from the dead),

units.leftText: and all the brothers who are with me, to the assemblies of Galatia:
units.rightText: and all the brethren that are with me, unto the churches of Galatia:
leftNotes: 1:2 The word for “brothers” here and where context allows may also be correctly translated “brothers and sisters” or “siblings.”

units.leftText: Grace to you and peace from God the Father and our Lord Jesus Christ,
units.rightText: Grace to you and peace from God the Father, and our Lord Jesus Christ,

units.leftText: who gave himself for our sins, that he might deliver us out of this present evil age, according to the will of our God and Father—
units.rightText: who gave himself for our sins, that he might deliver us out of this present evil world, according to the will of our God and Father:

units.leftText: to whom be the glory forever and ever. Amen.
units.rightText: to whom be the glory for ever and ever. Amen.

units.leftText: I marvel that you are so quickly deserting him who called you in the grace of Christ to a different “good news”,
units.rightText: I marvel that ye are so quickly removing from him that called you in the grace of Christ unto a different gospel;

units.leftText: but there isn’t another “good news.” Only there are some who trouble you and want to pervert the Good News of Christ.
units.rightText: which is not another gospel: only there are some that trouble you, and would pervert the gospel of Christ.

units.leftText: But even though we, or an angel from heaven, should preach to you any “good news” other than that which we preached to you, let him be cursed.
units.rightText: But though we, or an angel from heaven, should preach unto you any gospel other than that which we preached unto you, let him be anathema.

units.leftText: As we have said before, so I now say again: if any man preaches to you any “good news” other than that which you received, let him be cursed.
units.rightText: As we have said before, so say I now again, If any man preacheth unto you any gospel other than that which ye received, let him be anathema.

units.leftText: For am I now seeking the favor of men, or of God? Or am I striving to please men? For if I were still pleasing men, I wouldn’t be a servant of Christ.
units.rightText: For am I now seeking the favor of men, or of God? or am I striving to please men? if I were still pleasing men, I should not be a servant of Christ.

units.leftText: But I make known to you, brothers, concerning the Good News which was preached by me, that it is not according to man.
units.rightText: For I make known to you, brethren, as touching the gospel which was preached by me, that it is not after man.

units.leftText: For I didn’t receive it from man, nor was I taught it, but it came to me through revelation of Jesus Christ.
units.rightText: For neither did I receive it from man, nor was I taught it, but it came to me through revelation of Jesus Christ.

units.leftText: For you have heard of my way of living in time past in the Jews’ religion, how that beyond measure I persecuted the assembly of God and ravaged it.
units.rightText: For ye have heard of my manner of life in time past in the Jews’ religion, how that beyond measure I persecuted the church of God, and made havoc of it:

units.leftText: I advanced in the Jews’ religion beyond many of my own age among my countrymen, being more exceedingly zealous for the traditions of my fathers.
units.rightText: and I advanced in the Jews’ religion beyond many of mine own age among my countrymen, being more exceedingly zealous for the traditions of my fathers.

units.leftText: But when it was the good pleasure of God, who separated me from my mother’s womb and called me through his grace,
units.rightText: But when it was the good pleasure of God, who separated me, even from my mother’s womb, and called me through his grace,

units.leftText: to reveal his Son in me, that I might preach him among the Gentiles, I didn’t immediately confer with flesh and blood,
units.rightText: to reveal his Son in me, that I might preach him among the Gentiles; straightway I conferred not with flesh and blood:

units.leftText: nor did I go up to Jerusalem to those who were apostles before me, but I went away into Arabia. Then I returned to Damascus.
units.rightText: neither went I up to Jerusalem to them that were apostles before me: but I went away into Arabia; and again I returned unto Damascus.

units.leftText: Then after three years I went up to Jerusalem to visit Peter, and stayed with him fifteen days.
units.rightText: Then after three years I went up to Jerusalem to visit Cephas, and tarried with him fifteen days.

units.leftText: But of the other apostles I saw no one except James, the Lord’s brother.
units.rightText: But other of the apostles saw I none, save James the Lord’s brother.

units.leftText: Now about the things which I write to you, behold, before God, I’m not lying.
units.rightText: Now touching the things which I write unto you, behold, before God, I lie not.
leftNotes: 1:20 “Behold”, from “ἰδοὺ”, means look at, take notice, observe, see, or gaze at. It is often used as an interjection.

units.leftText: Then I came to the regions of Syria and Cilicia.
units.rightText: Then I came into the regions of Syria and Cilicia.

units.leftText: I was still unknown by face to the assemblies of Judea which were in Christ,
units.rightText: And I was still unknown by face unto the churches of Judæa which were in Christ:

units.leftText: but they only heard, “He who once persecuted us now preaches the faith that he once tried to destroy.”
units.rightText: but they only heard say, He that once persecuted us now preacheth the faith of which he once made havoc;

units.leftText: So they glorified God in me.
units.rightText: and they glorified God in me.

units.leftText: Then after a period of fourteen years I went up again to Jerusalem with Barnabas, taking Titus also with me.
units.rightText: Then after the space of fourteen years I went up again to Jerusalem with Barnabas, taking Titus also with me.

units.leftText: I went up by revelation, and I laid before them the Good News which I preach among the Gentiles, but privately before those who were respected, for fear that I might be running, or had run, in vain.
units.rightText: And I went up by revelation; and I laid before them the gospel which I preach among the Gentiles but privately before them who were of repute, lest by any means I should be running, or had run, in vain.

units.leftText: But not even Titus, who was with me, being a Greek, was compelled to be circumcised.
units.rightText: But not even Titus who was with me, being a Greek, was compelled to be circumcised:

units.leftText: This was because of the false brothers secretly brought in, who stole in to spy out our liberty which we have in Christ Jesus, that they might bring us into bondage,
units.rightText: and that because of the false brethren privily brought in, who came in privily to spy out our liberty which we have in Christ Jesus, that they might bring us into bondage:

units.leftText: to whom we gave no place in the way of subjection, not for an hour, that the truth of the Good News might continue with you.
units.rightText: to whom we gave place in the way of subjection, no, not for an hour; that the truth of the gospel might continue with you.

units.leftText: But from those who were reputed to be important—whatever they were, it makes no difference to me; God doesn’t show partiality to man—they, I say, who were respected imparted nothing to me,
units.rightText: But from those who were reputed to be somewhat (whatsoever they were, it maketh no matter to me: God accepteth not man’s person)—they, I say, who were of repute imparted nothing to me:

units.leftText: but to the contrary, when they saw that I had been entrusted with the Good News for the uncircumcised, even as Peter with the Good News for the circumcised—
units.rightText: but contrariwise, when they saw that I had been intrusted with the gospel of the uncircumcision, even as Peter with the gospel of the circumcision

units.leftText: for he who worked through Peter in the apostleship with the circumcised also worked through me with the Gentiles—
units.rightText: (for he that wrought for Peter unto the apostleship of the circumcision wrought for me also unto the Gentiles);

units.leftText: and when they perceived the grace that was given to me, James and Cephas and John, those who were reputed to be pillars, gave to Barnabas and me the right hand of fellowship, that we should go to the Gentiles, and they to the circumcision.
units.rightText: and when they perceived the grace that was given unto me, James and Cephas and John, they who were reputed to be pillars, gave to me and Barnabas the right hands of fellowship, that we should go unto the Gentiles, and they unto the circumcision;

units.leftText: They only asked us to remember the poor—which very thing I was also zealous to do.
units.rightText: only they would that we should remember the poor; which very thing I was also zealous to do.

units.leftText: But when Peter came to Antioch, I resisted him to his face, because he stood condemned.
units.rightText: But when Cephas came to Antioch, I resisted him to the face, because he stood condemned.

units.leftText: For before some people came from James, he ate with the Gentiles. But when they came, he drew back and separated himself, fearing those who were of the circumcision.
units.rightText: For before that certain came from James, he ate with the Gentiles; but when they came, he drew back and separated himself, fearing them that were of the circumcision.

units.leftText: And the rest of the Jews joined him in his hypocrisy, so that even Barnabas was carried away with their hypocrisy.
units.rightText: And the rest of the Jews dissembled likewise with him; insomuch that even Barnabas was carried away with their dissimulation.

units.leftText: But when I saw that they didn’t walk uprightly according to the truth of the Good News, I said to Peter before them all, “If you, being a Jew, live as the Gentiles do, and not as the Jews do, why do you compel the Gentiles to live as the Jews do?
units.rightText: But when I saw that they walked not uprightly according to the truth of the gospel, I said unto Cephas before them all, If thou, being a Jew, livest as do the Gentiles, and not as do the Jews, how compellest thou the Gentiles to live as do the Jews?

units.leftText: “We, being Jews by nature and not Gentile sinners,
units.rightText: We being Jews by nature, and not sinners of the Gentiles,

units.leftText: yet knowing that a man is not justified by the works of the law but through faith in Jesus Christ, even we believed in Christ Jesus, that we might be justified by faith in Christ and not by the works of the law, because no flesh will be justified by the works of the law.
units.rightText: yet knowing that a man is not justified by the works of the law but through faith in Jesus Christ, even we believed on Christ Jesus, that we might be justified by faith in Christ, and not by the works of the law: because by the works of the law shall no flesh be justified.

units.leftText: But if while we sought to be justified in Christ, we ourselves also were found sinners, is Christ a servant of sin? Certainly not!
units.rightText: But if, while we sought to be justified in Christ, we ourselves also were found sinners, is Christ a minister of sin? God forbid.

units.leftText: For if I build up again those things which I destroyed, I prove myself a law-breaker.
units.rightText: For if I build up again those things which I destroyed, I prove myself a transgressor.

units.leftText: For I through the law died to the law, that I might live to God.
units.rightText: For I through the law died unto the law, that I might live unto God.

units.leftText: I have been crucified with Christ, and it is no longer I who live, but Christ lives in me. That life which I now live in the flesh, I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave himself up for me.
units.rightText: I have been crucified with Christ; and it is no longer I that live, but Christ liveth in me: and that life which I now live in the flesh I live in faith, the faith which is in the Son of God, who loved me, and gave himself up for me.

units.leftText: I don’t reject the grace of God. For if righteousness is through the law, then Christ died for nothing!”
units.rightText: I do not make void the grace of God: for if righteousness is through the law, then Christ died for nought.

units.leftText: Foolish Galatians, who has bewitched you not to obey the truth, before whose eyes Jesus Christ was openly portrayed among you as crucified?
units.rightText: O foolish Galatians, who did bewitch you, before whose eyes Jesus Christ was openly set forth crucified?

units.leftText: I just want to learn this from you: Did you receive the Spirit by the works of the law, or by hearing of faith?
units.rightText: This only would I learn from you, Received ye the Spirit by the works of the law, or by the hearing of faith?

units.leftText: Are you so foolish? Having begun in the Spirit, are you now completed in the flesh?
units.rightText: Are ye so foolish? having begun in the Spirit, are ye now perfected in the flesh?

units.leftText: Did you suffer so many things in vain, if it is indeed in vain?
units.rightText: Did ye suffer so many things in vain? if it be indeed in vain.

units.leftText: He therefore who supplies the Spirit to you and does miracles among you, does he do it by the works of the law, or by hearing of faith?
units.rightText: He therefore that supplieth to you the Spirit, and worketh miracles among you, doeth he it by the works of the law, or by the hearing of faith?

units.leftText: Even so, Abraham “believed God, and it was counted to him for righteousness.”
units.rightText: Even as Abraham believed God, and it was reckoned unto him for righteousness.

units.leftText: Know therefore that those who are of faith are children of Abraham.
units.rightText: Know therefore that they that are of faith, the same are sons of Abraham.

units.leftText: The Scripture, foreseeing that God would justify the Gentiles by faith, preached the Good News beforehand to Abraham, saying, “In you all the nations will be blessed.”
units.rightText: And the scripture, foreseeing that God would justify the Gentiles by faith, preached the gospel beforehand unto Abraham, saying, In thee shall all the nations be blessed.

units.leftText: So then, those who are of faith are blessed with the faithful Abraham.
units.rightText: So then they that are of faith are blessed with the faithful Abraham.

units.leftText: For as many as are of the works of the law are under a curse. For it is written, “Cursed is everyone who doesn’t continue in all things that are written in the book of the law, to do them.”
units.rightText: For as many as are of the works of the law are under a curse: for it is written, Cursed is every one who continueth not in all things that are written in the book of the law, to do them.

units.leftText: Now that no man is justified by the law before God is evident, for, “The righteous will live by faith.”
units.rightText: Now that no man is justified by the law before God, is evident: for, The righteous shall live by faith;

units.leftText: The law is not of faith, but, “The man who does them will live by them.”
units.rightText: and the law is not of faith; but, He that doeth them shall live in them.

units.leftText: Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law, having become a curse for us. For it is written, “Cursed is everyone who hangs on a tree,”
units.rightText: Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law, having become a curse for us; for it is written, Cursed is every one that hangeth on a tree:

units.leftText: that the blessing of Abraham might come on the Gentiles through Christ Jesus, that we might receive the promise of the Spirit through faith.
units.rightText: that upon the Gentiles might come the blessing of Abraham in Christ Jesus; that we might receive the promise of the Spirit through faith.

units.leftText: Brothers, speaking of human terms, though it is only a man’s covenant, yet when it has been confirmed, no one makes it void or adds to it.
units.rightText: Brethren, I speak after the manner of men: Though it be but a man’s covenant, yet when it hath been confirmed, no one maketh it void, or addeth thereto.

units.leftText: Now the promises were spoken to Abraham and to his offspring. He doesn’t say, “To descendants ”, as of many, but as of one, “To your offspring”, which is Christ.
units.rightText: Now to Abraham were the promises spoken, and to his seed. He saith not, And to seeds, as of many; but as of one, And to thy seed, which is Christ.

units.leftText: Now I say this: A covenant confirmed beforehand by God in Christ, the law, which came four hundred thirty years after, does not annul, so as to make the promise of no effect.
units.rightText: Now this I say: A covenant confirmed beforehand by God, the law, which came four hundred and thirty years after, doth not disannul, so as to make the promise of none effect.

units.leftText: For if the inheritance is of the law, it is no more of promise; but God has granted it to Abraham by promise.
units.rightText: For if the inheritance is of the law, it is no more of promise: but God hath granted it to Abraham by promise.

units.leftText: Then why is there the law? It was added because of transgressions, until the offspring should come to whom the promise has been made. It was ordained through angels by the hand of a mediator.
units.rightText: What then is the law? It was added because of transgressions, till the seed should come to whom the promise hath been made; and it was ordained through angels by the hand of a mediator.

units.leftText: Now a mediator is not between one, but God is one.
units.rightText: Now a mediator is not a mediator of one; but God is one.

units.leftText: Is the law then against the promises of God? Certainly not! For if there had been a law given which could make alive, most certainly righteousness would have been of the law.
units.rightText: Is the law then against the promises of God? God forbid: for if there had been a law given which could make alive, verily righteousness would have been of the law.

units.leftText: But the Scripture imprisoned all things under sin, that the promise by faith in Jesus Christ might be given to those who believe.
units.rightText: But the scripture shut up all things under sin, that the promise by faith in Jesus Christ might be given to them that believe.

units.leftText: But before faith came, we were kept in custody under the law, confined for the faith which should afterwards be revealed.
units.rightText: But before faith came, we were kept in ward under the law, shut up unto the faith which should afterwards be revealed.

units.leftText: So that the law has become our tutor to bring us to Christ, that we might be justified by faith.
units.rightText: So that the law is become our tutor to bring us unto Christ, that we might be justified by faith.

units.leftText: But now that faith has come, we are no longer under a tutor.
units.rightText: But now that faith is come, we are no longer under a tutor.

units.leftText: For you are all children of God, through faith in Christ Jesus.
units.rightText: For ye are all sons of God, through faith, in Christ Jesus.

units.leftText: For as many of you as were baptized into Christ have put on Christ.
units.rightText: For as many of you as were baptized into Christ did put on Christ.

units.leftText: There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither slave nor free man, there is neither male nor female; for you are all one in Christ Jesus.
units.rightText: There can be neither Jew nor Greek, there can be neither bond nor free, there can be no male and female; for ye all are one man in Christ Jesus.

units.leftText: If you are Christ’s, then you are Abraham’s offspring and heirs according to promise.
units.rightText: And if ye are Christ’s, then are ye Abraham’s seed, heirs according to promise.

units.leftText: But I say that so long as the heir is a child, he is no different from a bondservant, though he is lord of all,
units.rightText: But I say that so long as the heir is a child, he differeth nothing from a bondservant though he is lord of all;

units.leftText: but is under guardians and stewards until the day appointed by the father.
units.rightText: but is under guardians and stewards until the day appointed of the father.

units.leftText: So we also, when we were children, were held in bondage under the elemental principles of the world.
units.rightText: So we also, when we were children, were held in bondage under the rudiments of the world:

units.leftText: But when the fullness of the time came, God sent out his Son, born to a woman, born under the law,
units.rightText: but when the fulness of the time came, God sent forth his Son, born of a woman, born under the law,

units.leftText: that he might redeem those who were under the law, that we might receive the adoption as children.
units.rightText: that he might redeem them that were under the law, that we might receive the adoption of sons.

units.leftText: And because you are children, God sent out the Spirit of his Son into your hearts, crying, “Abba, Father!”
units.rightText: And because ye are sons, God sent forth the Spirit of his Son into our hearts, crying, Abba, Father.
leftNotes: 4:6 Abba is a Greek spelling for the Aramaic word for “Father” or “Daddy” used in a familiar, respectful, and loving way.

units.leftText: So you are no longer a bondservant, but a son; and if a son, then an heir of God through Christ.
units.rightText: So that thou art no longer a bondservant, but a son; and if a son, then an heir through God.

units.leftText: However at that time, not knowing God, you were in bondage to those who by nature are not gods.
units.rightText: Howbeit at that time, not knowing God, ye were in bondage to them that by nature are no gods:

units.leftText: But now that you have come to know God, or rather to be known by God, why do you turn back again to the weak and miserable elemental principles, to which you desire to be in bondage all over again?
units.rightText: but now that ye have come to know God, or rather to be known by God, how turn ye back again to the weak and beggarly rudiments, whereunto ye desire to be in bondage over again?

units.leftText: You observe days, months, seasons, and years.
units.rightText: Ye observe days, and months, and seasons, and years.

units.leftText: I am afraid for you, that I might have wasted my labor for you.
units.rightText: I am afraid of you, lest by any means I have bestowed labor upon you in vain.

units.leftText: I beg you, brothers, become as I am, for I also have become as you are. You did me no wrong,
units.rightText: I beseech you, brethren, become as I am, for I also am become as ye are. Ye did me no wrong:

units.leftText: but you know that because of weakness in the flesh I preached the Good News to you the first time.
units.rightText: but ye know that because of an infirmity of the flesh I preached the gospel unto you the first time:

units.leftText: That which was a temptation to you in my flesh, you didn’t despise nor reject; but you received me as an angel of God, even as Christ Jesus.
units.rightText: and that which was a temptation to you in my flesh ye despised not, nor rejected; but ye received me as an angel of God, even as Christ Jesus.

units.leftText: What was the blessing you enjoyed? For I testify to you that, if possible, you would have plucked out your eyes and given them to me.
units.rightText: Where then is that gratulation of yourselves? for I bear you witness, that, if possible, ye would have plucked out your eyes and given them to me.

units.leftText: So then, have I become your enemy by telling you the truth?
units.rightText: So then am I become your enemy, by telling you the truth?

units.leftText: They zealously seek you in no good way. No, they desire to alienate you, that you may seek them.
units.rightText: They zealously seek you in no good way; nay, they desire to shut you out, that ye may seek them.

units.leftText: But it is always good to be zealous in a good cause, and not only when I am present with you.
units.rightText: But it is good to be zealously sought in a good matter at all times, and not only when I am present with you.

units.leftText: My little children, of whom I am again in travail until Christ is formed in you—
units.rightText: My little children, of whom I am again in travail until Christ be formed in you—

units.leftText: but I could wish to be present with you now, and to change my tone, for I am perplexed about you.
units.rightText: but I could wish to be present with you now, and to change my tone; for I am perplexed about you.

units.leftText: Tell me, you that desire to be under the law, don’t you listen to the law?
units.rightText: Tell me, ye that desire to be under the law, do ye not hear the law?

units.leftText: For it is written that Abraham had two sons, one by the servant, and one by the free woman.
units.rightText: For it is written, that Abraham had two sons, one by the handmaid, and one by the freewoman.

units.leftText: However, the son by the servant was born according to the flesh, but the son by the free woman was born through promise.
units.rightText: Howbeit the son by the handmaid is born after the flesh; but the son by the freewoman is born through promise.

units.leftText: These things contain an allegory, for these are two covenants. One is from Mount Sinai, bearing children to bondage, which is Hagar.
units.rightText: Which things contain an allegory: for these women are two covenants; one from mount Sinai, bearing children unto bondage, which is Hagar.

units.leftText: For this Hagar is Mount Sinai in Arabia, and answers to the Jerusalem that exists now, for she is in bondage with her children.
units.rightText: Now this Hagar is mount Sinai in Arabia and answereth to the Jerusalem that now is: for she is in bondage with her children.

units.leftText: But the Jerusalem that is above is free, which is the mother of us all.
units.rightText: But the Jerusalem that is above is free, which is our mother.

units.leftText: For it is written,
units.rightText: For it is written,

units.leftText: Now we, brothers, as Isaac was, are children of promise.
units.rightText: Now we, brethren, as Isaac was, are children of promise.

units.leftText: But as then, he who was born according to the flesh persecuted him who was born according to the Spirit, so also it is now.
units.rightText: But as then he that was born after the flesh persecuted him that was born after the Spirit, so also it is now.

units.leftText: However, what does the Scripture say? “Throw out the servant and her son, for the son of the servant will not inherit with the son of the free woman.”
units.rightText: Howbeit what saith the scripture? Cast out the handmaid and her son: for the son of the handmaid shall not inherit with the son of the freewoman.

units.leftText: So then, brothers, we are not children of a servant, but of the free woman.
units.rightText: Wherefore, brethren, we are not children of a handmaid, but of the freewoman.

units.leftText: Stand firm therefore in the liberty by which Christ has made us free, and don’t be entangled again with a yoke of bondage.
units.rightText: For freedom did Christ set us free: stand fast therefore, and be not entangled again in a yoke of bondage.

units.leftText: Behold, I, Paul, tell you that if you receive circumcision, Christ will profit you nothing.
units.rightText: Behold, I Paul say unto you, that, if ye receive circumcision, Christ will profit you nothing.

units.leftText: Yes, I testify again to every man who receives circumcision that he is a debtor to do the whole law.
units.rightText: Yea, I testify again to every man that receiveth circumcision, that he is a debtor to do the whole law.

units.leftText: You are alienated from Christ, you who desire to be justified by the law. You have fallen away from grace.
units.rightText: Ye are severed from Christ, ye who would be justified by the law; ye are fallen away from grace.

units.leftText: For we through the Spirit, by faith wait for the hope of righteousness.
units.rightText: For we through the Spirit by faith wait for the hope of righteousness.

units.leftText: For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision nor uncircumcision amounts to anything, but faith working through love.
units.rightText: For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision availeth anything, nor uncircumcision; but faith working through love.

units.leftText: You were running well! Who interfered with you that you should not obey the truth?
units.rightText: Ye were running well; who hindered you that ye should not obey the truth?

units.leftText: This persuasion is not from him who calls you.
units.rightText: This persuasion came not of him that calleth you.

units.leftText: A little yeast grows through the whole lump.
units.rightText: A little leaven leaveneth the whole lump.

units.leftText: I have confidence toward you in the Lord that you will think no other way. But he who troubles you will bear his judgment, whoever he is.
units.rightText: I have confidence to you-ward in the Lord, that ye will be none otherwise minded: but he that troubleth you shall bear his judgment, whosoever he be.

units.leftText: But I, brothers, if I still preach circumcision, why am I still persecuted? Then the stumbling block of the cross has been removed.
units.rightText: But I, brethren, if I still preach circumcision, why am I still persecuted? then hath the stumbling-block of the cross been done away.

units.leftText: I wish that those who disturb you would cut themselves off.
units.rightText: I would that they that unsettle you would even go beyond circumcision.

units.leftText: For you, brothers, were called for freedom. Only don’t use your freedom as an opportunity for the flesh, but through love be servants to one another.
units.rightText: For ye, brethren, were called for freedom; only use not your freedom for an occasion to the flesh, but through love be servants one to another.

units.leftText: For the whole law is fulfilled in one word, in this: “You shall love your neighbor as yourself.”
units.rightText: For the whole law is fulfilled in one word, even in this: Thou shalt love thy neighbor as thyself.

units.leftText: But if you bite and devour one another, be careful that you don’t consume one another.
units.rightText: But if ye bite and devour one another, take heed that ye be not consumed one of another.

units.leftText: But I say, walk by the Spirit, and you won’t fulfill the lust of the flesh.
units.rightText: But I say, Walk by the Spirit, and ye shall not fulfil the lust of the flesh.

units.leftText: For the flesh lusts against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh; and these are contrary to one another, that you may not do the things that you desire.
units.rightText: For the flesh lusteth against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh; for these are contrary the one to the other; that ye may not do the things that ye would.

units.leftText: But if you are led by the Spirit, you are not under the law.
units.rightText: But if ye are led by the Spirit, ye are not under the law.

units.leftText: Now the deeds of the flesh are obvious, which are: adultery, sexual immorality, uncleanness, lustfulness,
units.rightText: Now the works of the flesh are manifest, which are these: fornication, uncleanness, lasciviousness,

units.leftText: idolatry, sorcery, hatred, strife, jealousies, outbursts of anger, rivalries, divisions, heresies,
units.rightText: idolatry, sorcery, enmities, strife, jealousies, wraths, factions, divisions, parties,

units.leftText: envy, murders, drunkenness, orgies, and things like these; of which I forewarn you, even as I also forewarned you, that those who practice such things will not inherit God’s Kingdom.
units.rightText: envyings, drunkenness, revellings, and such like; of which I forewarn you, even as I did forewarn you, that they who practise such things shall not inherit the kingdom of God.

units.leftText: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faith,
units.rightText: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, kindness, goodness, faithfulness,

units.leftText: gentleness, and self-control. Against such things there is no law.
units.rightText: meekness, self-control; against such there is no law.

units.leftText: Those who belong to Christ have crucified the flesh with its passions and lusts.
units.rightText: And they that are of Christ Jesus have crucified the flesh with the passions and the lusts thereof.

units.leftText: If we live by the Spirit, let’s also walk by the Spirit.
units.rightText: If we live by the Spirit, by the Spirit let us also walk.

units.leftText: Let’s not become conceited, provoking one another, and envying one another.
units.rightText: Let us not become vainglorious, provoking one another, envying one another.

units.leftText: Brothers, even if a man is caught in some fault, you who are spiritual must restore such a one in a spirit of gentleness, looking to yourself so that you also aren’t tempted.
units.rightText: Brethren, even if a man be overtaken in any trespass, ye who are spiritual, restore such a one in a spirit of gentleness; looking to thyself, lest thou also be tempted.

units.leftText: Bear one another’s burdens, and so fulfill the law of Christ.
units.rightText: Bear ye one another’s burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ.

units.leftText: For if a man thinks himself to be something when he is nothing, he deceives himself.
units.rightText: For if a man thinketh himself to be something when he is nothing, he deceiveth himself.

units.leftText: But let each man examine his own work, and then he will have reason to boast in himself, and not in someone else.
units.rightText: But let each man prove his own work, and then shall he have his glorying in regard of himself alone, and not of his neighbor.

units.leftText: For each man will bear his own burden.
units.rightText: For each man shall bear his own burden.

units.leftText: But let him who is taught in the word share all good things with him who teaches.
units.rightText: But let him that is taught in the word communicate unto him that teacheth in all good things.

units.leftText: Don’t be deceived. God is not mocked, for whatever a man sows, that he will also reap.
units.rightText: Be not deceived; God is not mocked: for whatsoever a man soweth, that shall he also reap.

units.leftText: For he who sows to his own flesh will from the flesh reap corruption. But he who sows to the Spirit will from the Spirit reap eternal life.
units.rightText: For he that soweth unto his own flesh shall of the flesh reap corruption; but he that soweth unto the Spirit shall of the Spirit reap eternal life.

units.leftText: Let’s not be weary in doing good, for we will reap in due season if we don’t give up.
units.rightText: And let us not be weary in well-doing: for in due season we shall reap, if we faint not.

units.leftText: So then, as we have opportunity, let’s do what is good toward all men, and especially toward those who are of the household of the faith.
units.rightText: So then, as we have opportunity, let us work that which is good toward all men, and especially toward them that are of the household of the faith.

units.leftText: See with what large letters I write to you with my own hand.
units.rightText: See with how large letters I write unto you with mine own hand.

units.leftText: As many as desire to make a good impression in the flesh compel you to be circumcised, just so they may not be persecuted for the cross of Christ.
units.rightText: As many as desire to make a fair show in the flesh, they compel you to be circumcised; only that they may not be persecuted for the cross of Christ.

units.leftText: For even they who receive circumcision don’t keep the law themselves, but they desire to have you circumcised, so that they may boast in your flesh.
units.rightText: For not even they who receive circumcision do themselves keep the law; but they desire to have you circumcised, that they may glory in your flesh.

units.leftText: But far be it from me to boast except in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, through which the world has been crucified to me, and I to the world.
units.rightText: But far be it from me to glory, save in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, through which the world hath been crucified unto me, and I unto the world.

units.leftText: For in Christ Jesus neither is circumcision anything, nor uncircumcision, but a new creation.
units.rightText: For neither is circumcision anything, nor uncircumcision, but a new creature.

units.leftText: As many as walk by this rule, peace and mercy be on them, and on God’s Israel.
units.rightText: And as many as shall walk by this rule, peace be upon them, and mercy, and upon the Israel of God.

units.leftText: From now on, let no one cause me any trouble, for I bear the marks of the Lord Jesus branded on my body.
units.rightText: Henceforth let no man trouble me; for I bear branded on my body the marks of Jesus.

units.leftText: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit, brothers. Amen.
units.rightText: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit, brethren. Amen.
